title: P34: ALiBi (per-head linear distance bias, slopes 1/2..1/256) replaces RoPE in all six Peri-LN blocks, on the 107-claude Lean incumbent (4.80M params)
description: Idea ID: P34 (ALiBi, Press et al. 2021, 'train short, test long'). Every block's attention drops the rotary rotation of q and k and instead adds -slope_h * (query pos - key pos) to the logits through SDPA's additive mask, slopes 2^-1..2^-8 for the 8 heads, no new parameters (4,800,000), persisting into RL and eval; the KV-cache path stores key positions so cached decoding matches the full forward (CPU-checked). Pretraining sees only cap-6 chains while RL and eval need 7-12 lines, which is exactly ALiBi's designed regime: a relative recency prior that extrapolates by construction, and 111-fable showed removing RoPE's 12 strided rotations per forward buys ~44% more pretraining steps and ~35% faster sampling, which NoPE then wasted by losing the position signal at unseen lengths.
hypothesis: 111-fable (NoPE) fit cap-6 Lean chains as well as RoPE (val loss 0.0825 vs 0.0822) with 44% more steps, but its round-1 RL start was much worse (targets solved 556/568/464 vs 722/689/679, sample acc 0.21 vs 0.29 at lengths 7+ even though parse failures matched), so the deficit was position information that does not extrapolate from the causal mask alone. RoPE extrapolates poorly too (rotary angles at positions past the training range are unseen; Press et al. 2021 show RoPE perplexity blowing up beyond train length while ALiBi stays flat). ALiBi supplies a position signal that is a pure function of relative distance with no learned or trained-range-dependent component: head 1 (slope 1/2) is near-local, head 8 (slope 1/256) is effectively global, so retrieval of far premises stays possible while local Lean syntax (which slot of 'have nK : P := rule nI nJ') gets a strong recency cue at every length. Prediction if right: pretraining steps ~4,300-4,700 (like 111: no apply_rope; the bias is one (1,8,T,T) tensor per forward plus one bf16 cast per block), final val loss at or below 107's 0.0822/0.0827/0.0836 thanks to the extra steps, round-1 targets solved at or above 107's 722/689/679 (NoPE: 556/568/464), RL rounds 200-260 s (faster sampling), and a metric above 587. Evidence against: ALiBi has been reported to underperform RoPE in-distribution at scale and its recency prior may hurt citation of premises many lines back; the float SDPA mask drops the flash kernel for the memory-efficient one (fine at T~250, d_head 32); 058-claude's one-layer NoPE probe found the cap-6 length prior strengthened, so position encoding may not be what limits length transfer at all. Mechanism checks: (a) steps vs 107's 3264/3208/3277 and 111's 4716/4704/4706; (b) round-1 targets solved and sample acc vs both; (c) RL-solved r1->r4 gain vs 107's +371 and 111's +403; (d) eval L* and the ge histogram at 10-12 vs 107 (82/16/3).
expected_delta: -45 to +45 dev solves >= 7 vs 107-claude's 587.00 (central +8); pretraining steps 4,300-4,700 (107: 3264/3208/3277; 111 NoPE: 4716/4704/4706), final val loss 0.077-0.086; totals 1,400-1,800 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and CHANGED: ALiBi positional bias instead of RoPE (P34)
arch.pos: alibi (CHANGED from rope: no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/8) = 1/2, 1/4, ..., 1/256 for heads 1..8, Press et al. 2021 defaults; -inf for masked/future keys)
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 107-claude: (1) PeriLNBlock.attn is the fork Block.attn with the apply_rope(q)/apply_rope(k) line removed and SDPA called with attn_mask = the float ALiBi bias cast to q.dtype (no is_causal path; causality is -inf in the bias); qkv/proj/KV-cache handling, Peri-LN, width, heads, depth, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, optimizer and schedule unchanged. (2) the model is ALiBiGPT, a GPT subclass whose forward skips rope_cache and builds the bias once per forward: pos = arange (training/val, bias shape (1,8,T,T) broadcast over the batch) or the given pos (sample.generate's left-padded batches); key positions are stored in caches[0]['pos'] for incremental decoding; the given bool mask (causal + key padding) is applied as -inf, so pads-attend-to-self rows stay finite. Slopes are a non-persistent buffer (not in state_dict). ALiBi persists into RL and eval
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 107-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107), no parameters added or removed; slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from pretrain.py, replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys as 107). A plain fork GPT would load the weights but apply RoPE, giving a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: fork attn/cache code copied unchanged minus the rotation, one cache dict per model.blocks index; caches[0] additionally holds key positions. CPU check with the pinned fork 51604b3: left-padded 2-sequence prefill plus 4 cached one-token steps vs the unpadded full forward, max abs logit diff < 1e-4; training loss/backward run

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
